LESSON PLAN CRE ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The difference between the Bible and other books.
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to differentiate the bible from other books as a holy book used by
Christians.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What is the bible?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Cooperation Interpersonal relationships
 collaboration  Holiness Effective communication
  Imagination and  Respect, responsibility
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Children’s bible.
Other books.
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 20-21.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners to page 20 of the learner’s book. Allow them to look at the picture before taking them
 through the questions on page 21.
 Step 2: Display the two bible and other books and ask the learners to identify the Bible.
 Step 3: Ask the learners to explain why the bible is special.
 Step 4: Lead learners to sing the song. Encourage them to dramatize.
SUMMARY
Learners to read out summary notes to complete the explanation
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to read summary notes with family members.

 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The people who wrote the Bible
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to able to explain how the writing of the bible was different from other
books and respect it.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Who wrote the bible?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Cooperation Effective communication
 collaboration  Holiness
  Learning to learn  Respect, responsibility
LEARNING RESOURCES
Pictures of the first pages of the bible.
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 20-21.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners to read 2 Timothy 3:16 .
 Step 2: Ask learners what they understand from the Bible verse. Lead them to conclude that the bible was written
 by people who were guided by God.
 Step 3: Guide learners in pairs or groups to do activity 3.
 Step 4: Ask learners to say what they feel about the Bible.
SUMMARY
Learners to read out summary notes to complete the explanation
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to read summary notes with family members.

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Books of the New Testament
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to:-
 a. State the number of books in the New Testament and develop interest to read them.
 b. Name the four Gospel books in the New Testament and relate them to the teaching of Jesus Christ.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How many books are in the New Testament?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Cooperation Effective communication
 collaboration 
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES
Flash cards with names of books of the New Testament.
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 23-24.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners to read 2 Timothy 3:16
 Step 2: Ask learners what they understand from the Bible verse. Lead them to conclude that the bible was written
 by many people
 Step 3: Guide learners in pairs or groups to do activity 5.
 Step 4: Encourage the learners to read the Gospel books with the assistance of parents or other adults.
SUMMARY
Learners to read out summary notes to complete the explanation
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to read summary notes with family members.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The story of Moses and the burning bush
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to narrate what happened in the story of Moses and the burning bush and
relate it with the Holy places of worship.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What happened to Moses at Mount Sinai?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Obedience Effective communication
 collaboration  Responsibility Assertiveness
  Learning to learn  Humility Decision making
  Digital literacy  Holiness
LEARNING RESOURCES
Video of Moses and the burning bush.
Laptop, a projector.
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 26-28.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners question of Activity 1.
 Step 2: Guide learners to look at the pictures then attempt to answer questions that follow.
 Step 3: Guide learners in pairs or groups to read Exodus 3:1-6.
 Step 4: Narrate/read the story from the bible as they follow the picture sequence in the learner’s book.
SUMMARY
Learners to read out summary notes to complete the explanation.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to attend a Bible club if the school has one and participate in the activities.

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Moses obeyed God
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to discuss how Moses expressed obedience and apply it in their lives
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How did Moses show obedience to God?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Obedience Interpersonal relationships
 collaboration  Decision making
  Learning to learn
  Imagination and
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Props and costumes for the role play.
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 29-30.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners through activity 5 and ask learners what they do when they are called.
 Step 2: Guide learners to read Exodus 3:1-6.
 Step 3: Guide learners to role play the story of Moses.
 Step 4: Ask learners to point out how Moses showed obedience to God in the story. Put the learners in group and
 ask them to discuss the question in activity 6.
SUMMARY
Learners to read out summary notes to complete the explanation
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to practice keeping each other accountable when it comes to being obedient..

 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The story of Jonah and the big fish
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to narrate the story of Jonah and be obedient to God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How did Jonah disobey God? What was the result of Jonah’s disobedience?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Obedience Effective communication
 collaboration  Respect Decision making
  Learning to learn  Forgiveness
  Imagination and  Responsibility
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 31-33.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners through activity 1 and ask learners the questions.
 Step 2: Guide learners to the pictures under activity 1 and lead them through looking at the pictures and reading
 text.
 Step 3: Guide learners to read Jonah 1:1-4, 15, 17; 2:10.
 Step 4: Direct learners through activity 2 and ask them to narrate the story of Jonah.
SUMMARY
Lead learners to appreciate the miracle of Jonah being swallowed and spit out unarmed, by the fish.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to practice making a fish mosaic of obedience.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Jonah is punished by God
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to explain the results of Jonah’s disobedience and desire to obey God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What happened to Jonah when he disobeyed God?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Obedience Effective communication
 collaboration  Respect Decision making
  Learning to learn  Forgiveness
  Imagination and  Responsibility
 creativity  Love
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Papers on which are written scenarios where children were obedient and others disobedient to God, their parents and
their teachers.
Learner’s Book 3 page 33-34.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners to say what happens when they disobey. Guide them to do activity 3 on page 33.
 Step 2: Guide learners to read Jonah 1:4, 15, 17
 Step 3: Ask learners to try and explain how Jonah disobeyed God and what happened he disobeyed
 Step 4: Lead the learners to identify the lesson they learn from the disobedience of Jonah and its consequences
 Step 5: Learners should make commitment to forgive others just as God forgave Jonah.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to practice making a fish mosaic of obedience.

Review the previous lesson.

Learners to read summary notes.

Learners to ask and answer questions and explain the take home activity

Learners to practice making a fish mosaic of obedience.

Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to describe the healing of Naaman and desire to have faith in God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What happened to Jonah when he disobeyed God?
 Core competencies Values PCIs

 collaboration  Humility Decision making

 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Props and costumes for the role-play.
Learner’s Book 3 page 35-36.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Introduce the lesson by asking learners to name different diseases they know by asking them the first
 activity in Activity.
 Step 2: Ask learners to look at the pictures and read the words in the pictures in part 2 of activity 1.
 Step 3: Guide learners to read 2 Kings 5:1-14
 Step 4: Using questions guide the learners to understand that Naaman was healed because he had faith In God and
 because he followed instructions.
 Step 5: Ask learners what they learn from the story and how they will apply what they have learned.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions and explain the take home activity

Learners to participate in health programmes in the school.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: God heals us
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to appreciate God as the healer of all diseases.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Who heals you when you are sick?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Obedience Effective communication
 collaboration  Humility Decision making
  Learning to learn  Faith Self-esteem
   Persistence Health education
  Social justice
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Mirrors or other reflective surfaces.
A chart showing different people being treated in hospital
Learner’s Book 3 page 36-37.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners to activity 4 in the learner’s book page 36.
 Step 2: Ask learners if they have ever been in unwell and what happened so that they could get better.
 Step 3: Lead learners to the understanding that it is God who ultimately healed Naaman. Elisha was used by God to
 heal Naaman.
 Step 4: Through questions, lead learners to commit to have faith in God to heal them when they are unwell. Ask
 them how they can show this faith.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Review the lesson
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to participate in health programmes in the school.

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The story of the three Hebrew men
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to narrate the story of the three Hebrew men and strengthen their
relationship with God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What happened to the three Hebrew men? Who rescued the three Hebrew men from fire?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Trust Effective communication
 collaboration  Faith Decision making
  Learning to learn  Courage assertiveness
  Imagination and
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Laptop, projector, video of the story.
Learner’s Book 3 page 38-39.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners to name the various local communities In Kenya that they know.
 Step 2: Direct learners to questions 1 in activity 1.
 Step 3: Point learners to part 2 of activity 1. Give them time to look at the pictures
 Step 4: Guide to read the bibles verses and lead them realization that the three Hebrew men refused to worship a
 statue and were thrown into the fire.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to sing a song that covers the story of the three Hebrew men.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to participate in a fire drill for the whole school.

 Step 2: Let learners to state the lessons they learn from the story and explain how they will apply them in their
 lives.
 Step 3: Ask learners questions to evaluate how well they have understood the key details of the story.
 Step 4: Guide learners to have faith and trust in God in their own lives.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to sing a song that covers the story of the three Hebrew men.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to participate in a fire drill for the whole school.
